> Status: draft. This vignette follows the official pyUCell tutorials; it has
> not been run on representative data.

Score supplied gene signatures in one AnnData object, inspect the scores, and
save the object, tables, and figures. Install the required packages in your
Python environment before opening the notebook:

```bash
pip install pyucell scanpy matplotlib
```

## 1. Load the expression object

Use an `.h5ad` with unique cell and gene IDs, a raw `counts` layer, and a
`cluster` column. Keep the full measured gene space rather than only highly
variable genes. Gene IDs must match the signatures below; these examples use
human gene symbols.

```{python}
#| label: load-expression

from pathlib import Path
from importlib.metadata import version

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scanpy as sc
import pyucell as uc
from scipy import sparse

adata = ad.read_h5ad("input/processed_single_cell.h5ad")
assert adata.n_obs > 0 and adata.n_vars > 0
assert adata.obs_names.is_unique and adata.var_names.is_unique
assert "counts" in adata.layers and "cluster" in adata.obs
assert not adata.obs["cluster"].isna().any()
counts = adata.layers["counts"]
values = counts.data if sparse.issparse(counts) else np.asarray(counts)
assert np.isfinite(values).all() and (values >= 0).all()
print(adata)
print("pyucell version:", version("pyucell"))

output = Path("output/pyucell")
output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

The explicit layer prevents scoring a scaled or integrated `adata.X` by
accident. Per-cell normalization and `log1p` preserve within-cell ranks;
scaling each gene across cells changes those ranks. If raw counts are in
`adata.X`, preserve them as `adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()` before
preprocessing.

## 2. Define signatures and inspect gene coverage

Replace these small marker examples with your biological signatures. A `+`
suffix marks a positive gene and a `-` suffix marks a negative gene; genes
without a suffix are positive. Each signature needs measured genes for every
direction it includes.

```{python}
#| label: define-signatures

signatures = {
    "Tcell": ["CD3D", "CD3E", "CD2"],
    "Bcell": ["MS4A1", "CD79A", "CD79B"],
    "CD8T": ["CD8A+", "CD8B+", "CD4-"],
}

coverage = pd.DataFrame(
    [(name, gene.rstrip("+-"), "negative" if gene.endswith("-") else "positive")
     for name, genes in signatures.items() for gene in genes],
    columns=["signature", "gene", "direction"],
)
coverage["present"] = coverage["gene"].isin(adata.var_names)
print(coverage.groupby(["signature", "direction"])["present"].agg(["sum", "count"]))
print(coverage.loc[~coverage["present"]])
assert coverage.groupby(["signature", "direction"])["present"].any().all()
coverage.to_csv(output / "signature_gene_coverage.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
```

Missing genes change the interpretation of a signature. The scoring cell uses
`missing_genes="impute"`, which assigns missing genes the lowest rank. The
alternative `"skip"` removes them from the signature. Choose deliberately
after inspecting coverage, especially for targeted gene panels.

## 3. Score cells from the counts layer

`max_rank` caps the ranked gene list. The example keeps the default 1500, capped
at the measured gene count; inspect detected genes per cell before changing
it. Keep the same gene space and scoring settings when comparing datasets.

```{python}
#| label: score-signatures

detected_genes = np.asarray((counts > 0).sum(axis=1)).ravel()
print(pd.Series(detected_genes).describe())
max_rank = min(1500, adata.n_vars)
assert max_rank > 1
score_columns = [f"{name}_UCell" for name in signatures]
assert not set(score_columns).intersection(adata.obs.columns), "Scores already exist"

uc.compute_ucell_scores(
    adata,
    signatures=signatures,
    layer="counts",
    max_rank=max_rank,
    missing_genes="impute",
    w_neg=1.0,
    chunk_size=500,
    n_jobs=1,
)
scores = adata.obs[score_columns]
assert np.isfinite(scores.to_numpy()).all()
assert ((scores >= 0) & (scores <= 1)).all().all()
print(scores.describe())
```

Scores are added to `adata.obs`. For signed signatures, pyUCell subtracts the
weighted negative score from the positive score and clips negative results to
zero. These scores describe signature enrichment; they are not cell-type
probabilities or evidence of pathway flux.

## 4. Plot scores by cluster and on an existing UMAP

Use the embedding already associated with the processed object. The UMAP
cell is optional when `adata.obsm["X_umap"]` is absent.

```{python}
#| label: plot-signature-scores

sc.pl.violin(adata, keys=score_columns, groupby="cluster", rotation=90, show=False)
plt.gcf().savefig(output / "ucell_by_cluster.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

if "X_umap" in adata.obsm:
    figure = sc.pl.umap(
        adata, color=score_columns, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=1,
        return_fig=True, show=False,
    )
    figure.savefig(output / "ucell_umap.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()
```

Clusters summarize cells, while biological replication belongs to samples or
donors. A condition comparison needs a design that accounts for those samples.
Optional kNN smoothing is described in the upstream tutorial; retain original
scores alongside smoothed scores because smoothing borrows information from
the chosen neighbors.

## 5. Save the scored object and settings

```{python}
#| label: save-ucell-results

adata.uns["pyucell_vignette"] = {
    "version": version("pyucell"),
    "signatures": signatures,
    "layer": "counts",
    "max_rank": max_rank,
    "missing_genes": "impute",
    "w_neg": 1.0,
    "ties_method": "average",
    "chunk_size": 500,
    "n_jobs": 1,
}
adata.obs[score_columns].rename_axis("cell_id").reset_index().to_csv(
    output / "ucell_scores.tsv", sep="\t", index=False,
)
adata.write_h5ad(output / "single_cell_ucell.h5ad")
```
